data.why: CosmOracle needs no external dataset; the scientist enters a redshift and cosmological parameters (H0, Omega_m, Omega_k, w0, wa) directly in the sidebar form.

goals: Compute the comoving, transverse comoving, luminosity, and angular-diameter distances to a chosen redshift under a chosen cosmology
Compute the lookback time and comoving volume out to that redshift
Compute the physical size of an object subtending 1 arcsecond at that redshift
Compare how distance measures diverge across cosmic history by plotting them (linear or semi-log) over a redshift range
Export the computed distance-measure table to a text file for later analysis

review.summary: The tree describes CosmOracle just as the README does: compute the distance measures, volume, lookback time and 1-arcsec scale at z under a preset or custom cosmology, plot them over 0..z, and export the table. The evidence in 14 checked screens holds up, with one partial (003). It needs light restructuring before filing: put redshift entry in the setup phase, fold the per-chart option tasks into one plotting task, drop the bad-input and fullscreen nodes, and add the Definitions page as a feature.
